title: Annotatio IV §.VIII open: Fourth century — Nicene Fathers’ complexus and the Marchic Reformed formula
pass_a_gloss: §. VIII. About to advance my foot to examine the Testimonies of the FOURTH age, I cannot but remember first of all that most excellent complexus of Testimonies of this kind, conceived in the words of the NICENE FATHERS, opening the sentence of the whole Christian Church of that time concerning the Sacred supper; and so much the more to remember, the more certainly the words of the Formula of administering the Sacred Supper received in our Reformed Marchic Churches and others, immediately preceding the administration itself, seem to be owed to that complexus — by which Communicants are admonished not so far to cling in their thoughts to the Sacred Symbols most evidently set before the senses in the Sacred Supper, but truly to direct the eyes of the mind to Heaven, and surely and more surely, nay by divine faith, to establish and hold that their souls are no less fattened by the very true and substantial body and blood of Christ than the Sacred Symbols are assumed and perceived by the mouth of the body.
pass_b_english: §.VIII: stepping into the FOURTH century, first remember the Nicene Fathers’ complexus — opening the whole Church’s sentence on the Sacred Supper.

Our Marchic Reformed administration formula seems drawn from it: communicants must not cling to the sensed symbols, but lift the mind’s eyes to heaven and by divine faith hold that souls are fed by Christ’s true substantial body and blood no less than the mouth takes the symbols.
source_text: §. VIII. Ad QUARTI SECULI Testimonia excutienda pedem promoturus, non possum non meminisse primo omnium locô præstantissimi hujusmodi Testimoniorum complexûs, PATRUM NICÆNORUM verbis concepti, totiusque Ecclesiæ ejus temporis christianæ de S. cœna sententiam aperientis; tantóque magis meminisse, quantò certiùs Formulæ administrandi Cœnam S., in Ecclesiis nostris Reformatis Marchicis aliisque receptæ, verba, administrationem ipsam immediatè antecedentia, complexui isti accepta ferenda videntur, quibus nempe Communicantes admonentur, cogitationibus suis non usque adeò Symbolis Sacris, in S. Cœna sensibus evidentissimè expositis, inhærere, sed verò oculos mentis in Cœlum dirigere, certòque certiùs, quin fide divina, statuere atque tenere, animas suas non minus ipso corpore sanguineque Christi veris ac substantialibus, saginari, quàm Symbola S. ore corporis à se assumantur ac percipiantur.
